title: Add overload scenarios (step traffic + long-prompt spikes) and CI gating for p99 + error mix
author: Tomáš Novák
description:
Context: As part of the Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding rollout (ENG-4831 umbrella for perf validation), we need deterministic overload scenarios in perf-canary to (a) reproduce tail-latency collapse modes seen in incident spikes and (b) gate regressions on p99 latency and error composition. This PR adds two synthetic traffic profiles: (1) step-function traffic ramp (2x→6x in <30s) to validate early shedding and breaker stability; (2) long-prompt spike (prefill-heavy) to stress queueing + memory/KV-cache pressure. It also adds CI gating thresholds for p99 and error mix so we fail builds when we regress into ambiguous 5xx/timeouts instead of stable overload-protected responses.

What’s included: Adds new scenario definitions and a runner for “overload” profiles; integrates optional headers to tag tier/route to match admission control classification; records per-interval p95/p99, request timeouts, disconnects, and error code breakdown (HTTP + Redwood error codes when present); introduces gating rules: p99 ceiling per endpoint (streaming vs non-streaming), max timeout ratio, and max internal-5xx ratio; overload-protected errors (429/503 with Redwood overload codes + Retry-After) are allowed within a bounded band, but internal 5xx/502/timeouts are treated as regressions.

Defaults/gates (initial): - chat.completions (streaming): p99 <= 2.8s decode latency at baseline load; during overload window p99 <= 6.0s and no sustained upward slope for >2 intervals - chat.completions (non-streaming): p99 <= 5.5s baseline; overload window p99 <= 9.0s - timeouts: <0.25% baseline; <1.0% overload window - internal 5xx (excluding overload-protected): <0.10% baseline; <0.25% overload window - overload-protected responses (429/503 w/ Retry-After) allowed up to 12% in the overload window for the step scenario (tunable per env)

Notes: (1) These gates are intentionally conservative for the first week of canary to avoid blocking unrelated changes; we can tighten once we have a week of data. (2) Error taxonomy alignment: runner attempts to parse Redwood error payload ("code"/"type") if present, but remains compatible with older endpoints by classifying by HTTP status and presence of Retry-After. (3) Streaming: we separately track "disconnect" rate since customers reported disconnects under overload; we treat disconnects as timeouts for gating.

Rollout plan: Land in perf-canary first, run nightly against us-east canary cluster for 3 days, then enable required gating for PR checks once we confirm thresholds don’t flap (coordinating with ENG-4840 tuning).

Screenshots/Artifacts: Added sample output in docs/overload-scenarios.md and attached a CI run artifact showing the new summary table.

Testing: Verified locally with replay harness; ran against staging canary (us-east) with induced capacity limits; validated summary report and that gates fail when injecting artificial 5xx/timeouts.

Follow-ups: - Add a third scenario for “retry storm” (client-side) once SDK retry guidance ships (ENG-4836) - Tighten error-mix threshold post-canary and align with SLO accounting changes (SLO toolkit PR-204).
commits: runner: add overload scenario harness + summary tables
scenarios: step-function traffic profile w/ configurable plateau windows
scenarios: long-prompt spike profile (prefill heavy) + token distribution controls
metrics: record disconnects + classify as timeout for streaming gates
gating: introduce p99 + error-mix thresholds and CI failure reasons
docs: add overload scenarios guide and sample report output
conversation: Sergio Costa (review): Can we avoid adding model_id as a metric label? This will explode cardinality if folks run multi-model suites.
Tomáš Novák (author): Good call. Updated errors/latency metrics to emit model_class instead of model_id, and kept model_id only in the human-readable report. CI gates use model_class + endpoint only.
Amara Diallo (review): For the error-mix gate, how do we distinguish ‘good’ 503 (shed) from ‘bad’ 503 (upstream crash)? Not all 503s are equal.

Tomáš Novák (author): Implemented classification: 503 counts as overload-protected only if Retry-After is present OR payload contains Redwood overload code. Otherwise it is treated as internal 5xx for gating. Documented in docs/overload-scenarios.md.
Christine Wong (review): The step scenario ramp looks too abrupt (2x→6x in 10s). That might trigger breaker flapping in staging and cause noise. Can we parameterize ramp duration and add a plateau?

Tomáš Novák (author): Parameterized ramp_seconds + added plateau windows (default: 20s ramp, 2x baseline plateau 60s, overload plateau 120s). This matches the game-day playbook ramp shape we used last week.
Noah Patel (review): Long-prompt spike should also track prefill queue time separately from decode. Can we expose a ‘time_to_first_token’ percentile if streaming?

Tomáš Novák (author): Added TTFT (time_to_first_token_ms) calculation for streaming runs when chunk timings are available; included in the report but not gating yet. Follow-up suggested after we gather baseline data.

Tomáš Novák (author): Root cause was the runner treating gateway 502 from an intentionally killed upstream as “internal 5xx” but the scenario was configured with chaos enabled by default. I’ve disabled chaos defaults in overload suites and moved that into a separate experimental suite.
Sergio Costa (review): Thanks. With chaos off by default, I’m 👍. Please also log the gate decision reasons in a single line for easier triage in CI output.
Tomáš Novák (author): Added a one-line ‘GATE_FAIL: …’ summary with threshold + observed value. Rerunning CI.
Christine Wong (review): Approved after ramp/plateau change and clarified 503 classification.
Noah Patel (review): Approved. TTFT being reported is helpful; let’s keep gating limited until we establish baselines.
release_notes: perf-canary: Added overload traffic profiles (step ramp + long-prompt spikes) and CI gating on p99 latency + error composition to catch regressions into timeouts/internal 5xx during overload.
